 Delhi Schools To Remain Closed On November 16 For Chhath Puja 
 Delhi Schools To Remain Closed On November 16 For Chhath Puja
 BW Online Bureau
 Nov 14, 2026
 # Delhi schools holiday November 16 
 # Delhi school closure 
 # Chhath Puja 2026 
 # Delhi government schools 
 # private schools Delhi 
 # Directorate of Education Delhi 
 Delhi's Directorate of Education has declared November 16 a holiday for government, government-aided and recognised private schools following the state government's Chhath Puja notification
 All government, government-aided and recognised private schools in Delhi will remain closed on November 16 (Monday) on account of Chhath Puja, following a holiday notification issued by the Delhi Government. 
 The Directorate of Education (DoE), Delhi, has directed all schools and offices under its jurisdiction to observe the holiday in accordance with the government's notification declaring November 16 a public holiday for Pratihar Shashthi or Surya Shashthi, commonly known as Chhath Puja. 
 DoE Issues Holiday Circular 
 In its circular, the Directorate of Education directed all government schools, government-aided schools and unaided recognised private schools to remain closed on November 16. 
 The order also applies to all offices functioning under the Directorate of Education, Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi (GNCTD). 
 The circular stated, “In accordance with the aforesaid notification, it is hereby directed that all Government Schools, Government-Aided Schools, Unaided Recognised Private Schools, and all offices under the Directorate of Education, GNCTD, shall observe a holiday on 16th November, 2026 (Monday).” 
 Delhi Government Notifies Public Holiday 
 The directive follows an order issued by the General Administration Department of the Delhi Government, formally declaring November 16 a public holiday on account of Pratihar Shashthi or Surya Shashthi (Chhath Puja). 
 With the notification, the holiday has been extended to all government and recognised private schools across the national capital under the DoE's jurisdiction.
